comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** the URI fix is correct, and the new test catches the bug it targets. No issue was found in the production change within the tested scope. One point concerns coordination with open PR #12135: once both are merged, the new test no longer passes.

**Verified** by running the real base and head scripts (encoders, notifications and `wl-copy` stubbed) on 20 filenames and parsing the saved clipboard payload with GLib `g_filename_from_uri`, GIO `g_file_new_for_uri`, GTK's `text/uri-list` path, Qt `QMimeData::urls()` + `toLocalFile()`, Node's WHATWG `URL` with `fileURLToPath`, and the shell's clipboard history decoder:

| Output name contains | Base | Head |
|---|---|---|
| `#`, `?`, `#` in a parent directory, literal `%20` | misread by GLib, GIO, GTK, Qt and Node | exact path in every consumer |
| literal `%2F`, bare `%` | fails or misread in most consumers | exact path in every consumer |
| newline | payload splits into two entries | exact path in every consumer |
| only `A-Za-z0-9 _ . - ~ /` in the whole path (e.g. screen recording names) | exact path | byte-for-byte same payload as base |
| non-UTF-8 byte (`caf\xe9`) | wrong in every consumer | `%E9`: exact in GLib, GIO and GTK; Qt, Node's `fileURLToPath` and the history decoder cannot represent it (also wrong on base) |

Head was not worse than base for any tested name in any tested consumer.

**Verified**, also:
- **Test:** passes 15/15 on head, including with a `TMPDIR` containing `#` and a space, and under `test/shell`. On base it fails at "reserved characters are encoded rather than interpreted as URI syntax". It also catches five mutations: `-I` removed, `.resolve()` removed, `.absolute()` in place of `.resolve()`, `%` left unencoded, and `|| true` after the Python call.
- **`python3`:** present on standard installs. `uwsm`, `ufw`, `python-gobject` and `nautilus-python` in `install/omarchy-base.packages` all depend on `python`, and other `bin/` scripts already call `python3`.
- **`resolve()`:** gives the same path as `realpath --` for the output file, including relative paths through a symlinked directory.
- **Failure handling:** if the Python step fails, the script stops before `wl-copy` and before the success notification.

### New test fails when combined with #12135

The #13360 diff applies cleanly on top of #12135 (quality tiers), and #12135 does not touch `copy_to_clipboard`. In that combination #12135's own test still passes, but this PR's test fails at its first check:

```text
#12135:        "Saved and copied to clipboard${size:+ ($size)}."  ->  "Saved and copied to clipboard (<1 MB)."
this test:     grep -Fxq 'Saved and copied to clipboard.'          ->  no match  ->  not ok - successful copy reports completion
```

With only that match relaxed, the file stops at the first video case: #12135 prompts for quality when no fourth argument is given, and this test has no `omarchy-menu-select` stub. The run caught this with a tripwire stub; with Omarchy's own scripts on `PATH`, the real menu would be called from inside the test. With the relaxed match plus a menu stub, all 15 checks pass, so the encoding fix itself survives the combination. From reading only: the negative checks for clipboard and URI-conversion failures run after the output file exists, so under #12135 a regressed success message would carry a size, `! grep -Fq 'Saved and copied to clipboard.'` would not match it, and those two checks would pass without testing anything.

**Impact:** whichever of the two PRs lands second leaves `test/shell.d/transcode-clipboard-test.sh` failing until it is adjusted.

**Suggested change:** match the `Saved and copied to clipboard` prefix in both the positive and negative checks, and make the video cases answer the quality prompt: pass an explicit quality such as `medium` (the current command ignores a fourth argument), or add an `omarchy-menu-select` stub in `$scratch/bin` that prints `medium`. The stub variant was run and passes 15/15; the explicit-argument variant is from reading source. Tripwire stubs for `omarchy-menu-file` (and `omarchy-menu-select`, if the argument route is used) keep a real menu from ever opening inside the test. Open PR #6698 was also checked: its test and this one both pass when combined.

**Note:** `wl-copy --type text/uri-list` also offers the plain-text MIME types, so an app that pastes the plain-text type (as a terminal or plain text field may) now gets the encoded form (for example `Gr%C3%BC%C3%9Fe-high.png`) for names with spaces, non-ASCII or reserved characters. This is the correct URI text, but it may be visible to users (read from wl-clipboard source; no live paste was tested).

**Optional test improvement:** `check_uri` runs the command without `|| fail`, so the `-I` and `.resolve()` mutations above end the file through `set -e` with no `not ok` line (the runner still reports the file as failed). Adding `|| fail "$description"` after the `bash "$ROOT/bin/omarchy-transcode" ...` line names the failing case.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** PR test, mutations and payload parsing ran in an isolated command sandbox with Python 3.14.7, GLib 2.88.3 and Qt 6.11.2, with encoders, notifications and the clipboard stubbed. GTK 4.22.4's `text/uri-list` path was reproduced through the GLib calls it makes, and wl-clipboard 2.3.0 behaviour was read from source. Combinations with #12135 and #6698 were built locally from their current heads. Chromium/Electron handling was read from source only; Firefox was not examined. No live Wayland paste into a GUI application was performed, and no other Python version was run.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.
